subject: Request: availability exception & order form language for HeliumHealth MSA
messages:
From: Brett Cole <brett.cole@heliumhealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@heliumhealth.com
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: availability exception & order form language for HeliumHealth MSA

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the call yesterday — following up with the formal ask from our side. HeliumHealth is preparing to sign the MSA but we need a narrow availability exception written into the order form and a short SLA addendum attached to the MSA/SOW. Key asks are:

- Availability target: 99.99% for the /api/v1/clinical and /api/v1/ems endpoints, measured monthly.
- Latency target: 95th percentile < 200ms for those endpoints in us-east region (production traffic).
- Measurement: Redwood’s telemetry + our synthetic checks; we need the mechanics for shared measurement and a sample query for dispute windows.
- Credits: cap at 20% of monthly fees; credits calculated pro-rata for minutes of downtime beyond threshold.
- Multi-region failover: we will require at least one cross-region failover commitment and an incident playbook attached.

I've attached a short spreadsheet with the HeliumHealth requirements (Helium_Reqs_SLA.xlsx) and a marked-up MSA (MSA_Redlines_v1.docx). We understand this is an exception to standard terms — looking for a path forward and a final draft that procurement can sign.

Can you confirm what evidence you can provide for availability history (30/90/365 day windows) and whether Redwood is comfortable with the proposed credit cap? Also please share a timeline for when we can get a redline back.

Thanks,
Brett Cole
Director, Platform Ops
HeliumHealth
(415) 555-0182

Attachments: Helium_Reqs_SLA.xlsx (spreadsheet), MSA_Redlines_v1.docx (redlines)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Brett Cole <brett.cole@heliumhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 17:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: availability exception & order form language for HeliumHealth MSA

Hi Brett — thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. Really appreciate the specificity; that helps a lot.

Short answer: we can get you a bespoke order form + short SLA addendum, but we need to confirm a few internal items first (measurement windows, how credits are calculated, and whether we can commit to the 95th <200ms target consistently for both endpoints).

Plan:
- I’ve looped in Laura (sales ops) and Mina (legal) to draft order form language and a short SLA addendum that reference shared telemetry and a dispute process.
- Marcus (infra) will pull 30/90/365 day uptime and p95 latency extracts for the two endpoints in us-east and share as evidence.
- I will put together a proposed mutual action plan (MAP) with milestones: draft redline by Mon 12/21, internal legal review Tue 12/22, shared revision to Helium by Wed 12/23.

Can we schedule a 30-minute sync early next week to walk through the draft SLA and the measurement example? If you send a couple slot options I’ll lock it in.

I’ve attached an internal draft (redline-orderform-sla-draft.docx) that covers the basic pieces we typically agree to for limited exceptions — it’s intentionally narrow.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redline-orderform-sla-draft.docx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Dec 2026 08:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: availability exception & order form language for HeliumHealth MSA

Team — forwarding HeliumHealth’s asks and the materials they sent. High level items we need to land in language:

1) Definitions: define "Availability" (percentage of successful HTTP 2xx/3xx responses for production traffic to the listed endpoints) and the measurement window (UTC month).
2) Measurement & data sharing: Redwood provides telemetry extracts; Helium may run synthetic checks. For disputes, define a 72-hour review window and a sample query for their synthetic check results.
3) Credits calculation: pro-rata minutes beyond threshold, credits applied to next invoice, cap at 20% of monthly recurring charges (Helium proposed). Recommend adding a clause that caps total credits to the amount paid for the service in the prior month if procurement objects.
4) Latency SLO: p95 < 200ms for the two named endpoints in us-east; include language that SLO applies only to requests under a defined payload size and rate (so spikes from bulk imports don’t invalidate the SLO).
5) Multi-region failover commitment and incident playbook: attach a one-page playbook; Marcus can own the playbook content.

Marcus — can you pull the requested uptime and p95 extracts for the last 30/90/365 windows and put links in Drive (see related link)? We’ll need those as evidence for procurement.

Mina/Laura — I’ve attached our draft redline. Please comment on the credits cap and the suggested dispute mechanics. If Legal wants different wording for the credit cap, flag the exact substitute and I’ll run it with the customer.

Thanks — aiming to get a shared redline back to Helium by EOD Wed.

-Karthik

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Dec 2026 09:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: availability exception & order form language for HeliumHealth MSA

All — reviewed the draft. A few legal notes:

- Credits cap: 20% monthly cap is acceptable for a limited exception, but we should add a backstop that total credits will not exceed fees paid over the previous 30 days. That gives us a practical ceiling.
- Measurement: keep Redwood telemetry as the primary source and allow Helium synthetic checks to be rebuttal evidence. Define the dispute window as 14 calendar days to allow sufficient time to collect logs (72 hours is tight).
- Latency: include the payload/rate carve-out as suggested. Also exclude scheduled maintenance windows defined in the order form.
- Incident playbook: agree to provide a one-page playbook and a named escalation contact; do not commit to RTO beyond what our ops runbook supports.

I will apply these edits to the draft and remove any language that looks like an SLA warranty (keep it as an "SLA addendum" in the order form). Karthik — if Helium accepts the edits I will prepare a short signature block to append to the MSA (so the addendum is a standalone, attachable exhibit).

-Mina
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Brett Cole <brett.cole@heliumhealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@heliumhealth.com
Date: Tue, 21 Dec 2026 09:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: availability exception & order form language for HeliumHealth MSA

Karthik — this looks good, thanks. Our procurement team is okay with the 20% cap as long as the backstop doesn’t reduce Helium’s ability to claim credits for a major outage; they prefer the clean 20% but will accept the 30-day fees backstop if you must.

Next steps from our side: we’ll review Mina’s edits when you send them. If they are close to what you described, procurement can sign the order form with the SLA exhibit and we’ll route via DocuSign (link below). Can you also confirm you’ll attach the incident playbook and the telemetry extracts?

DocuSign (preview): https://docusign.com/helium/HL-2026-0923

Thanks — Brett

Attachments referenced: none in this message
